messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — serving-api-south1: high error-rate (5xx) and node flapping detected in rack-r4. Initial alert: 1800 req/s degraded, 12% tail latency spike.

sam: I'm on it. seeing a cluster-wide increase in retransmits on the RDMA fabric; multiple pods restarted with CUDA OOMs after failover.

maya: confirmed. kvcache miss rate exploded after node churn, then a handful of workers crashed w/ `CUDA out of memory` during KV rebuild.

lee: any customer-facing impact?

customer-success: customers A and B reporting timeouts; CS is triaging support tickets and will send updates.

sam: impact: 15% of requests returning 503/504 intermittently. Traffic is being rebalanced but retransmit churn causes service to thrash.

ops-bot: Runbook: Fabric flap -> isolate affected ToR, move traffic, scale down batch size. Steps suggested in #runbooks/serving-fabric.

maya: quick mitigation proposal: 1) pause new deploys 2) reduce global batch_size from 32 -> 4 3) pin serving to single-node fallback routing for affected customers 4) cordon + drain nodes in rack-r4

lee: +1 reduce batch_size ASAP. how do we pin routing?

sam: set route policy to `fallback-compact` for tenant groups 12/13 via console, and enable model-fallback to quantized-compat-7B. Doing that now.

sam: command: ``kubectl -n serving scale deployment/generator --replicas=0 --selector=rack!=r4`` to force move new work off r4 (run carefully).

maya: I'm running: ``kubectl -n serving cordon node/r4-node-12 && kubectl -n serving drain node/r4-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`` to evacuate.

eng-sre: we're seeing a NIC offload fallback causing bursts of reorders on ibx interfaces, looks like TSO/LSO bug on the driver after kernel update. Packets get reordered -> retransmit storm -> RDMA queue-depth bounce -> heap pressure during kvcache rebuild -> OOM.

sam: that matches logs: ``ibdev0: detected out-of-order >5000 pkts, qdepth surge`` followed by container restarts.

ops-bot: Suggested short term: disable large-seg offload on affected NICs to see if it improves ordering. Command: ``ethtool -K eth2 tso off gso off gro off`` (apply on ToR uplink and affected hosts via automation).

maya: applying ethtool on r4-node-*. Rolling across node 12 -> 13 -> 14. Monitoring.

lee: while that's rolling, let's reduce memory pressure on rebuilds: set kvcache.max_rebuild_parallelism=1 and kvcache.overflow_policy=reject (temp).

sam: changed kvcache flags via configmap and triggered rolling-restart of runtime with: ``kubectl -n serving rollout restart statefulset/llm-runtime`` (staggered).

customer-success: CS update: customers A and B notified of mitigation in progress. No SLA breaches yet but close. Will keep them notified every 30m.

maya: after disabling offloads on node-12, we saw retransmits drop 70% and OOMs stop for that host. Pushing to others.

eng-sre: good. latency down 30%, error-rate down to 6% from 15%. still seeing 503s from a subset behind r4-edge switch.

sam: next step: put r4 ToR into maintenance in fabric controller to avoid ECMP steering to flaky paths. Command: ``fabricctl mark-tor r4 --maintenance``. Doing now.

ops-bot: Reminder: enabling ToR maintenance will shift traffic to adjacent racks; watch for secondary congestion and kvcache misses.

maya: traffic shift observed. One worker in rack-r5 hit a short spike in memory for a single pod; I preemptively scaled replica count +1 for generator in r5 to smooth load.

taylor: should we short-circuit to smaller model for high QPS customers?

sam: yes, we've already enabled `fallback-compact` for the affected tenants. Rolling back to full models after fabric stabilized.

eng-sre: root cause hypothesis: recent NIC firmware + kernel combo introduced a pathological TSO behavior on certain mlx5 variants under microburst load. That amplifies ECMP asymmetry and triggers retransmit storms on the RDMA layer.

sam: action items: 1) continue offload-disable rollout to remaining racks 2) keep r4 in maintenance until vendor patch 3) schedule firmware rollback or vendor-supplied driver ASAP 4) postmortem to include timeline + customer impact + remediation.

maya: documenting commands and timeline in incident doc. Adding logs: ``[1746009999] ibq: reorder_count=5241; retransmit_ratio=0.42; kvcache_rebuilds=9``

customer-success: CS to record ticket IDs for affected accounts and include remediation ETA, will escalate to account owners.

taylor: any need to escalate to legal/compliance?

sam: not yet. no data plane exposure detected. We will escalate if SLA breaches expected.

ops-bot: On-call handoff in 2h. Current pager duty: sam -> maya at 18:15 UTC. Please update `#oncall` with status.

maya: I'll take the handoff. current status summary (to paste into #oncall): "Fabric-induced retransmit storm caused node flaps and transient CUDA OOMs; mitigations: disabled NIC offloads across affected hosts, cordoned/drained rack-r4, marked r4 ToR maintenance, reduced batch_size and kvcache rebuild parallelism, enabled model-fallback for impacted tenants. Error-rate reduced from 15% -> ~5-7%. CS notified."

sam: leaving detailed notes in incident doc and linking logs. If anything regresses ping me @sam.

eng-sre: tracking vendor support ticket and testing driver/firmware rollback in staging.

customer-success: will send a customer update in 20 minutes with current mitigations and expected next update time.

incident-bot: Incident severity remains P1. Handoff recorded: sam -> maya at 18:15 UTC. Please follow runbook and append findings to /incidents/1746009999/postmortem.md

maya: will monitor through the handoff window and capture all artifacts. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
